source.title: Size Doesn't Matter: Cosine-Scored Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study changes SAE encoder scoring and measures reconstruction error by token-norm quartile, bearing narrowly on whether SAE architecture affects reconstruction errors. It does not analyze the dark-matter error structure described in the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Q4 reconstruction results for different SAE scoring architectures, included below as evidence relevant only to V6. Its probing, interpretability, gradient, steering, and ablation results do not measure dark-matter predictability, cross-size context overlap, error-versus-random loss, or keeping the error term in analyses.
record.test_reason: The study never addresses dark matter, but it reports SAE reconstruction error under encoder-architecture changes on Qwen3-8B, in aggregate, by norm quartile, and with or without the dead-latent auxiliary loss. That bears narrowly on V6: whether error shrinks with better SAE design. It is not aimed at the dark-matter question, so T3 fits better than T5. V1–V5 are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that inner-product scoring conflates token norm with direction on normalized residual streams. A learned cosine score keeps aggregate reconstruction, KL and CE matched while improving sparse probing by about 14.6%, mainly through discovering features the standard SAE never learns. The standard SAE's reconstruction fails on high-norm tokens. They recommend cosine scoring by default for normalized, especially RMSNorm, models, while noting it does not hold universally: deep LayerNorm layers and sentiment are exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper changes SAE encoder-score geometry and reports norm-stratified reconstruction; it does not use the dark-matter decomposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Q4 reconstruction outcome changes with encoder scoring architecture; the paper also reports that effects depend on layer and model family.
record.peer_reviewed: Spotlight paper at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability
record.problems: The Q4 reconstruction evidence is for a single model, layer, and norm quartile in the headline setting. It does not measure the structure or predictability of the residual error vector, and the paper notes that some cross-model coverage uses shorter token budgets.
record.rows_left_out: No other SAE reconstruction rows were included: other reported reconstruction results were not specifically norm-stratified Q4 outcomes relevant to the narrow V6 connection, or were architecture and budget sweeps outside that comparison.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from input activations is not measured.
Not tested: per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, overlap of failing contexts, and persistence of error with scale.
There is no comparison of SAE-reconstruction loss against random errors of equal norm. KL and CE scores are reported, but with no random-error baseline.
The error is not decomposed into linear and nonlinear parts.
No circuit or steering analysis keeps or drops the error term.

Not tested: whether the linear or nonlinear dark-matter components change with architecture, and the effects of end-to-end training, the sparsity-penalty selectors JumpReLU/gated (explicitly untested) and shrinkage. Only encoder-score variants under fixed-k selectors were studied.

missing.what: Aggregate FVE at the headline setting for all four architectures (0.770, 0.769, 0.771, 0.767), plus KL and CE scores. This shows the total error is unchanged by the architecture change.
Q1–Q3 per-quartile FVE, matched across architectures (0.732–0.778).
No-auxiliary-loss FVE and dead-latent comparisons: Qwen L9/L18/L27 at 50M tokens; Gemma L7/L13/L19; 500M L27 with +6.3% FVE.
Dictionary-size control: standard 49k at k=240 reaches FVE 0.751 vs cosine 16k at 0.737, and standard 16k at 0.658.
Score swap at inference cuts FVE by about 0.11 in both directions, showing reconstruction is bound to the training score.

record.verdict_notes: The paper neither cites nor uses the dark-matter framework, so its bearing on V6 is indirect: it reports reconstruction error under architectural variation. The key fact for V6 cuts both ways. An architecture fix removes a large high-norm-tail error, but aggregate error is unchanged at matched recipe, so most error is not reduced by this design change. The per-quartile FVE magnitude for Q4 is inflated by within-quartile normalization. The record's single limits_scope label lumped together conditions that point in different directions; I have split it.

versions.untested_parts: Whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
Whether per-token error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
No comparison of model loss under SAE reconstruction versus random errors of the same size.
No decomposition of error into learned-feature and nonlinear components, nor a test of further dictionary learning on those components.
No test of whether SAE-based analyses lose behavior when the reconstruction error term is omitted.

The study tests an encoder-scoring architecture change and its effect on norm-stratified reconstruction, but not whether dark matter is mostly an artifact of sparsity penalties, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective choice; it does not establish that dark matter generally reflects training rather than representation structure.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Train a standard BatchTopK SAE with inner-product encoder scoring and report Q4 reconstruction.
rows.locator: Appendix G.1, Table 19; Appendix G, Q4 reconstruction
rows.note: The paper also reports a 9.5× reconstruction-norm/output-norm ratio on Q4 for the Standard SAE.
rows.check: This is the standard-SAE baseline (Q4 FVE −183.5), not an effect on its own. It is the reference for r2–r4, so 'observed' is wrong. Q4 FVE is normalized by small within-quartile variance (footnote 4), so the magnitude overstates Q4's share of total error.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix G.1, Table 19; Section 4.2; Appendix J, Table 21.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Train an adaptive cosine SAE with a global learned exponent and report Q4 reconstruction.
rows.note: Aggregate FVE is reported as matched with the Standard SAE.
rows.check: Valid for the high-norm quartile only. Q1–Q3 FVE is unchanged (0.732–0.777 vs 0.738–0.778), and aggregate FVE is 0.769 vs 0.770.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix G.1, Table 19, Global a column; Appendix D, Table 7.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Train a per-feature adaptive cosine SAE with base-plus-delta exponents and report Q4 reconstruction.
rows.note: Aggregate FVE is reported as matched with the Standard SAE.
rows.check: Same caveat as r2: the Q4 error is largely removed (0.252 vs −183.5), but aggregate and Q1–Q3 error do not shrink.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix G.1, Table 19, Per-feat. column; Section 3, base-plus-delta parameterization.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Train a magnitude-bypass SAE with norm restoration and report Q4 reconstruction.
rows.note: This architecture improves substantially over Standard on Q4 but its Q4 FVE remains below zero.
rows.check: Q4 improves greatly but stays negative (−0.200). Magnitude-bypass is single-seed.

source_check.correct: state: observed for the tested Q4 error-shrinkage component of V6. Magnitude-bypass Q4 FVE is −0.200 versus −183.5 for Standard.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix G.1, Table 19; Appendix D and Appendix K for single-seed status.
source_check.problem: Negative final FVE does not establish a partial architectural effect: Q4 reconstruction error falls dramatically, and V6 specifies no positive-FVE threshold.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-8B L18, 500M tokens, highest-norm token quartile (Q4), global and per-feature cosine scoring
relationships.reason: Changing only the encoder score turns Q4 FVE from −183.5 to 0.33/0.25. The high-norm-tail error is therefore an artifact of inner-product scoring (r1, r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Changing only encoder scoring raised highest-norm-quartile FVE from −183.5 to 0.33 with global cosine scoring and 0.25 with per-feature cosine scoring.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen3-8B L18, 500M tokens, highest-norm token quartile (Q4), global and per-feature cosine scoring
source_check.reason: Table 19 verifies r1–r3: Q4 FVE changes from −183.5 to 0.329 and 0.252, supporting an architectural origin for this specific error.

relationships.reason: Q4 error is reduced a lot, but Q4 FVE stays below zero (−0.200), so the tail error is only partly removed (r4).
relationships.display_finding: Magnitude bypass substantially reduced highest-norm-quartile error, but FVE remained below zero at −0.200.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Rows r1 and r4 show a dramatic reduction in Q4 error. Remaining negative FVE indicates imperfect reconstruction relative to within-quartile variance, but does not negate V6's prediction that better architecture shrinks error.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-8B L18, 500M tokens, aggregate error with the auxiliary dead-latent loss on
relationships.reason: From the text (no row): aggregate FVE is 0.770 standard vs 0.769/0.771/0.767 for the cosine variants. The total error does not shrink with the architecture change, and Q1–Q3 error is matched.
relationships.display_finding: Aggregate FVE was 0.770 for standard scoring versus 0.769, 0.771, and 0.767 for cosine variants, with matched error across the lower three norm quartiles.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Qwen3-8B L18, 500M tokens, aggregate error with the auxiliary dead-latent loss on
source_check.reason: Appendix D, Table 7 reports aggregate FVE 0.770 versus 0.769/0.771/0.767, explicitly treated as reconstruction parity. The tested architecture changes do not materially reduce aggregate error.

relationships.condition: No auxiliary dead-latent loss, Qwen3-8B 50M tokens (dsae 16k) and Gemma-2-2B 50M tokens
relationships.reason: From the text (no row): per-feature cosine raises FVE by +3.5/+1.6/+7.6% across layers and cuts dead latents, with Gemma FVE +3.9 to +6.7%. The error reduction appears only where dead latents are unmitigated.
relationships.display_finding: Without auxiliary dead-latent loss, per-feature cosine scoring increased Qwen3-8B FVE by 3.5%, 1.6%, and 7.6% across layers and Gemma-2-2B FVE by 3.9–6.7%, while reducing dead latents.

source_check.reason: Section 4.4 reports incomplete aggregate improvements and recipe dependence: Qwen per-feature FVE gains are +3.5/+1.6/+7.6%; Gemma's global Adaptive Cosine gains are +3.9 to +6.7%. relation.reason: Controlled encoder-architecture comparisons directly measure whether SAE reconstruction error shrinks, narrowly testing V6.

tranche.reason: The results qualify V6 through strong Q4 improvement, aggregate reconstruction parity with auxiliary loss, and aggregate gains without it. Their relevance is a condition-dependent restatement of V6 rather than simply a new setting.

source_check.notes: The exact checkpoint is Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base. Q4 results use a representative seed and within-quartile variance normalization; they neither establish aggregate error reduction nor test the linear/nonlinear dark-matter decomposition.

statements.correction: Standard Q4 FVE: −183.5; magnitude-bypass Q4 FVE: −0.200; magnitude-bypass: single seed; substantial architectural reduction of Q4 error; narrow support for V6's error-shrinkage component.
statements.problem: The numerical description and single-seed qualification are correct; the limits_scope classification does not follow merely from final Q4 FVE remaining negative.
